 JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one, (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 Smt.Sarojamma W/o Shankar.R, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 28.02.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, the said Sarojamma was proceeding as passenger along with his husband/petitioner in the Auto rickshaw came from Kallahalli Village to Bengaluru, while they reached Malekoppalu Flyover, near Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, at that time Lorry bearing No.TN-29-BU-3015 parked without any sign board and precautions in road side.
Due to this wrong parking of the lorry, Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AL-5863 was dashed to the offending lorry.
Due to which the said Sarojamma was sitting as passenger sustained grievous injuries as well as auto was damaged.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken first aid treatment at Government hospital,
Channarayapatna and Hassan and later she was shifted to Victoria hospital,
Bengaluru.
The said Sarojamma was treated as inpatient from 28.02.2024 to 01.03.2024 at Chamarajendra hospital, Hassan and from 01.03.2024 to 04.03.2024 at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.
Due to accidental injuries she was died on 04.03.2024.

The (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/-
towards obsequies ceremony and prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 60 years and was a Cloth and Flower vendor and earning more than Rs.50,000/- p.m.
The respondent No.3 is the daughter of the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner and respondent No.3 are facing acute financial crunch and both have lost love and affection of the deceased.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry and in this regard the Channarayapatna Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the offending lorry.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,

are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioner and respondent No.3 together with Shankar R vs Palani on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31699361/
2 cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections.
The respondent No.3 is the daughter of the deceased.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 denied issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry, alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending lorry, age, avocation and income of deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not in possession of valid driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle and there is no valid permit, fitness certificate to the offending lorry, hence, there is violation of policy conditions by the owner and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES
01. Whether petitioner proves that he is the LRs/dependent of deceased Smt.Sarojamma W/o Shankar.R?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Smt.Sarojamma W/o Shankar.R was died on 8.07.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, near Malekoppalu Flyover, NH-075,
Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-29-BU-3015 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether respondent No.2 proves that driver of lorry not having valid license?
04. Whether respondent No.2 proves that due to the negligence of the deceased vehicle auto rikshaw.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation?
05. Whether respondent No.2 proves that Auto rikshaw No.KA-03-AL-6863 owner and Insurance Company are necessary parties?
06. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
07 . What order or award?

 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner in his affidavit stated that the deceased Sarojamma is his wife.
To prove the said fact, he has produced notarized copy of Aadhaar card of himself as per Ex.P.8, which shows that petitioner is the husband of the deceased.
There is no dispute regarding relationship of the petitioner with the deceased in his cross-examination.
Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner is the legal representative and dependent on the income of the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

11. Issues No.2 and 4:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
12.
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief- examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

In his cross-examination he stated that he was working as auto driver, now he is not working and he was the owner of Auto bearing No.KA- 03-AL-5863 and in the said auto his wife also sitting and one Abhishek was driving the auto and admits that he and his wife were going as a passenger and the accident road is two way and having divider in the center of the road and admits that usually the lorries was parking on the side of the road and he has no children and the respondent No.3 Bhagyalakshmi is her wife first husband's daughter.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR with Complaint registered at Channarayapatna Traffic Police against driver of the offending Lorry for his negligent parking on the road.

Ex.P.2 is Charge sheet shows after (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of Auto rickshaw as A1 and owner/driver of the Lorry as A2, for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338, 304(A) of IPC Shankar R vs Palani on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31699361/
4 and Sec.122, 177 of MV Act, for the reasons that the driver of Auto rickshaw drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against rear portion of the lorry which was parked without any precautionary measures and caused the accident.
Due to which the driver of Auto rickshaw died on the spot.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on near the land of Devaraju Mallenahalli, Malekoppalu flyover, NH-75 Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report which discloses involvement of both vehicles in the accident and more damages caused to the Auto rickshaw.
It is opined that the said accident was not due to any mechanical defects of motor vehicles.
Ex.P.6 is Inquest report of deceased Sarojamma.
Ex.P.7 is PM report of deceased Sarojamma shows the cause of death is due to head injury sustained.
On going through the above said documents, it is clear that the accident occurred due to some (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 negligence on the part of the driver of Auto rickshaw.

Therefore,
it is clear that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the Auto rickshaw also this accident occurred.
Hence, some contributory negligence taken on the part of the petitioner's Auto rickshaw driver in the accident, but major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the offending lorry.
Accordingly, apportion of the negligence on the part of the deceased Auto rickshaw driver is taken at 40% and 60% on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry.
To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence.
Accordingly, Issues No.2 and 4 are answered partly in the affirmative.

13. Issues No.3 and 5:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.

14. The respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that driver of the offending Lorry was not having valid licence and petitioner has not made owner and insurer of his Auto rickshaw as necessary parties.

On perusal of Charge sheet, it is found that the Investigation Officer has not quoted any sections (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the driver of the offending lorry and further in the Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has clearly stated that the driver of Auto rickshaw who was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and he also contributed for the accident and has filed Charge sheet against deceased driver as accused No.1.
But the petitioner has not made owner and insurer of his Auto rickshaw as necessary parties.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 is acceptable.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the negative and Issue No.5 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.6:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Sarojamma, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 60 years and was a Cloth and Flower vendor and earning more than Rs.50,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.50,000/- towards obsequies ceremony.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner and respondent No.3 are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

sentences.text:
Since deceased was aged about 60 years and was working as self employee at the time of accident, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,500 +
1,650) = Rs.18,150/-.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are two dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then her monthly income would be (Rs.18,150 - Rs.6,050) = Rs.12,100/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.12,100/-.
As the (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 deceased was aged about 60 years, the multiplier of 9 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimant and respondent No.3 would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.12,100 x 12 x 9) Rs.13,06,800/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.

Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner and respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,58,900/- (Rupees Eight lakhs fifty eight thousand and nine hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner being the husband and respondent No.3 being the daughter of the deceased were (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.6097/2024 apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-30, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioner and respondent No.3 are meager one, they are entitled to get release their entire share amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details on proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
